Evidence: Japan will keep its borders closed to most foreign citizens through February as it prepares for an omicron surge, according to Prime Minister Fumio Kishida (Source 1 and Source 2). The country briefly eased border controls in November but reinstated them after the emergence of the omicron variant. Kishida stated that these stringent controls have helped slow the variant's spread and bought time for preparations. Japan is also accelerating booster shots for the elderly and expanding hospital capacity in response to rising COVID-19 cases (Source 1 and Source 2).
Justification: The retrieved evidence clearly states that Japan is maintaining border controls rather than lifting them. Sources 1 and 2 confirm that Japan will keep its borders closed to most foreign citizens through February as a measure to prepare for the omicron surge. This directly contradicts the claim that Japan has lifted border controls.
